summaries.summary: A2A is an open agent-to-agent protocol created by Google and now a Linux Foundation project (Apache 2.0), which joined the Agentic AI Foundation in August 2026. The current spec is v1.0.0, with JSON-RPC, gRPC and REST bindings, operations such as SendMessage and GetTask, and an Agent Card at /.well-known/agent-card.json. v1.0 renamed methods and removed implicit and password OAuth flows. Clients that send no A2A-Version header are treated as 0.3.

ACCOUNTADMIN is Snowflake's top account-level system role and contains SYSADMIN and SECURITYADMIN. Snowflake OAuth and External OAuth block it by default unless the privileged-roles blocked-list parameter is set to FALSE. It always has Cortex model access, and it controls account-wide AI settings: USE AI FUNCTIONS grants, Cortex Analyst enablement, cross-region inference, AI Guardrails, Snowflake Intelligence creation and PrivateLink authorization.

ApplicationIntegrationToolset is the Google ADK toolset (Python and Java) that connects agents to Application Integration workflows and Integration Connectors. It needs roles/integrations.integrationEditor, roles/connectors.invoker and roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor. Do not grant roles/integrations.integrationInvoker to agents on Agent Runtime: the docs say it can cause 403 errors.

The ADK CLI is Google ADK's command-line tool: adk for Python and adkgo for Go. adk deploy cloud_run and adk deploy agent_engine (adkgo deploy cloudrun and agentengine in Go) deploy agents to Cloud Run or Agent Runtime, and adkgo cloudrun deploys turn on --a2a by default. ADK also has a local API server, web UI and visual builder, but some command names such as adk web are unverified.

Agent Bricks is the umbrella name for Databricks' agent developer platform, which replaced the Mosaic AI Agent Framework name; its docs were rewritten for code-first agents on 2026-10-05. Its components include the Agent Bricks CLI, Agent Runtime (which hosts the agent server at an authenticated endpoint), Databricks Sandbox, Unity Gateway, Foundation Model APIs, Lakebase memory, MCP tools, AI Search, Genie Agents, MLflow and Unity Catalog. Databricks recommends Omnigent for multi-agent coordination.

The Agent Bricks CLI is Databricks' tool for scaffolding, running locally and deploying custom code agents to the agent runtime, in Beta since 2026-09-29 with no workspace preview toggle needed. Install it with uv or pip (databricks-agentbricks); it needs Python 3.11+ and the Databricks CLI on PATH, and projects are configured in agent.toml. Its templates are LangGraph and the OpenAI Agents SDK, and its commands include login, init, dev, deploy, memory, tools and mcp.

Agent Gateway is Google's policy enforcement point in the Govern pillar of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, governing ingress and egress LLM, MCP and A2A traffic for Agent Runtime and Gemini Enterprise (GA since 2026-06-25). It denies traffic by default and enforces IAM Unified Access Policies, IAP, Model Armor and Agent Registry, with up to 5,000 resources per gateway. VPC egress and static IP are GA, and cross-cloud support is in Limited Preview. Directly registered A2A agents bypass its policies.

Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) is a Google-created Apache 2.0 protocol for payments that agents start, built as an extension to A2A, MCP and UCP. The current version is v0.2, which uses Checkout and Payment mandates, and x402 samples exist. The specification is being donated to the FIDO Alliance.

Agent Platform Memory Bank is Google's managed long-term memory service for agents on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, renamed from Memory Bank on 2026-04-22. Gemini 3.5 Flash has been its default generation model since 2026-06-29. IngestEvents and memory profiles went GA in July 2026, and a console page was added in November 2026. Memory Bank and Sessions accept the global, us and eu locations.

Provisioned Throughput is Google's reserved-capacity option for models on Agent Platform, bought in GSUs on terms from 1 week to 1 year that can't be cancelled; ordering it needs roles/aiplatform.provisionedThroughputAdmin. Quota is GSUs times per-model throughput, and traffic over quota spills to pay-as-you-go by default unless the request-type header is set to dedicated, which returns a 429 instead. Fine-tuned model support went GA on 2026-11-04, and global endpoint coverage is unconfirmed.

The Agent Platform REST API is Google's API for Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. It kept the aiplatform.googleapis.com host after the rename, with regional hosts as LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com and us and eu multi-region jurisdictions; eu excludes the UK and Switzerland. Calls authenticate with an OAuth 2.0 bearer token, and in express mode an API key also works.

roles/aiplatform.user, titled Agent Platform User, is the Google Cloud IAM role that gives use access to most Agent Platform resources, including aiplatform.endpoints.predict. It is the baseline day-one role on the project, it is needed to deploy to Agent Runtime, and a custom Agent Runtime service account likely needs it plus whatever the agent code requires.

Agent Registry is Google Cloud's catalog of agents, MCP servers, tools, endpoints and skills, GA since 2026-06-18; it works with Agent Gateway, needs its API enabled in a governance project, reads A2A Agent Cards and supports A2A 1.0 and 0.3. Cloud Run MCP deploys and API hub register MCP servers in it automatically, and it replaced the gcloud MCP command groups. Microsoft also has an Agent Registry: the tenant-wide agent inventory in the Microsoft 365 admin center, programmable through Graph.

Agent Search, renamed from Vertex AI Search on 2026-04-22, is Google's managed enterprise search and grounding product, which runs on the Discovery Engine API. Its roles keep the discoveryengine names (admin, editor, user, viewer), and its service agent holds roles/discoveryengine.serviceAgent. Data stores are structured or unstructured, and connectors either federate or ingest. It has a remote MCP endpoint and lists FedRAMP, ISO, SOC, PCI DSS and HIPAA compliance (HIPAA needs a BAA).

Agent Toolkit for AWS is AWS's toolkit for AI agents working with AWS. It includes the AWS MCP Server and agent skills installed with npx skills add aws/agent-toolkit-for-aws/skills, including a migration skill for Bedrock Agents Classic. The awslabs/mcp README calls it the production successor to those servers.

A2A (Agent2Agent) is the cross-vendor agent interoperability protocol. Many platforms support it: AgentCore Runtime (server protocol A2A, port 9000), Foundry Agent Service (v1.0 GA, v0.3 preview), Copilot Studio connected agents, Work IQ, Google Agent Runtime (preview for multi-agent systems), Cloud Run, Agent Registry, MuleSoft Agent Fabric and Oracle Autonomous Database. Several services default to v0.3 unless the A2A-Version: 1.0 header is sent. No A2A support was found in the Databricks or OpenAI API docs reviewed, and Agentforce support is unconfirmed.

The AgentCore Runtime execution role is the AWS IAM role an agent on AgentCore Runtime assumes; it trusts bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com, with aws:SourceAccount and aws:SourceArn conditions against confused-deputy use. Its permissions cover ECR image pulls, CloudWatch Logs, X-Ray, CloudWatch metrics in the bedrock-agentcore namespace, workload access tokens and Bedrock model invocation. Direct code deployment agents use the same role without ECR statements, and auto-creating it from the console needs iam:CreateRole, CreatePolicy and AttachRolePolicy.

Agentforce is Salesforce's agent platform, formerly Einstein Copilot; admins with Manage AI Agents or similar permissions enable it, create agent users and set up ECAs. Actions (Apex, Flows, prompt templates, external services) must resolve to registered invocable actions at deploy time. It has a native MCP client, a headless REST Agent API and USD $2 per-conversation pricing. Limits of 20 agents per org and 15 topics per agent come from secondary sources, and A2A support is unconfirmed.

The Agentforce Agent API is Salesforce's REST API for headless agents, under api.salesforce.com/einstein/ai-agent/v1 (api.gov.salesforce.com for Government Cloud). Auth uses an External Client App with the client credentials flow, JWT-based tokens and scopes including chatbot_api and sfap_api, with tokens minted against the My Domain. Sessions run as the agent user or as the token user depending on bypassUser. Calls consume credits and time out after 120 seconds, and agents of type Agentforce (Default) are not supported.

The Agentforce agent user is the dedicated Salesforce identity that Agentforce Service Agents run as. It uses the Einstein Agent license and the Einstein Agent User profile, does not consume a seat, and can't log in interactively. It gets the AgentforceServiceAgentUserPsg permission set group, the Agentforce Service Agent Secure Base permission set and an agent-specific permission set for object access. Custom permission sets must fit the Einstein Agent license, and builder permissions should stay off this user.

Agentforce Builder is Salesforce's in-org agent builder inside Agentforce Studio, and using it requires the Manage AI Agents permission. The new builder is GA and available in Developer Edition orgs, and its Canvas and Script views both edit Agent Script. Secondary sources disagree on whether GA came in Spring '26 or Summer '26, and the reported legacy-builder retirement in the week of 2026-07-13 is unconfirmed.

The Agentforce MCP client is Salesforce's native client for calling external MCP servers from Agentforce. Admins register servers in the Agentforce Registry and allow the tools they want, and builders assign tools per subagent. Auth can be per-user OAuth, a client-credentials service account (which Salesforce warns is all-or-nothing), named credentials or none. Secondary sources say it was a pilot in 2025 and beta in January 2026; no official GA date was found.

Agentforce Vibes is Salesforce's IDE coding assistant, formerly Agentforce for Developers; the rename date is unconfirmed. Since April 2026, Claude Sonnet 4.5 is its default coding model in Developer Edition. Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers are documented for use in Agentforce Vibes.

Agents CLI (google-agents-cli) is Google's tool to scaffold, evaluate, deploy, publish and observe agents; it was at version 1.14.0 on 2026-11-12. Install it with uvx or uv tool install. agents-cli deploy targets Agent Runtime, Cloud Run and GKE, and --agent-identity deploys with Agent Identity. agents-cli publish gemini-enterprise publishes an agent to Gemini Enterprise.

AI_EXTRACT is a Snowflake Cortex AI Function for extracting information from documents, and it uses the arctic-extract model with token billing. It replaced Document AI: the Document AI UI and !PREDICT were retired on 2026-03-16, and migrated legacy models are called with AI_EXTRACT(model => ..., file => ...). Page filtering was added on 2026-11-10.

Amazon Bedrock is AWS's serverless model service; models are enabled by default and activate on first call through AWS Marketplace permissions. Auth uses IAM SigV4 or API keys against the bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints, with PrivateLink and managed policies such as AmazonBedrockFullAccess. Throttling is by TPM and RPM per model and Region, with recent Claude output tokens counted at 5:1. It doesn't train on customer data, covers FedRAMP Moderate, SOC and HIPAA, and Claude there lacks some Anthropic API features.

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is AWS's agent platform, GA since October 2025 and in GovCloud since May 2026, with 13 modular services (including Harness, Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Policy and Registry) that work with any framework or model. It supports PrivateLink through three interface endpoints, whose policies can only filter IAM principals, plus VPC egress. It is managed through the AgentCore CLI, CDK, CloudFormation and Terraform. Pricing is consumption-based per component, and it is in scope for SOC.

The AgentCore CLI is AWS's npm tool (@aws/agentcore, v1.0.3, Node 20.12 or later) for creating, deploying and invoking AgentCore agents and gateways. Deploying needs CDK stack access, permission to pass roles and resource-creation rights; AWS advises pre-bootstrapped least-privilege CDK roles in production. Gateway inbound auth defaults to NONE if --authorizer-type is omitted. On Windows, the old pip agentcore command can shadow it.

AgentCore Gateway is AWS's managed MCP gateway, combining Lambda, API Gateway, OpenAPI, Smithy, remote MCP and 16 built-in integration targets into one MCP server, and it can also route LLM traffic. Inbound auth is CUSTOM_JWT, IAM (bedrock-agentcore:InvokeGateway), AUTHENTICATE_ONLY or NONE, chosen at creation, and AWS warns against NONE in production. Outbound auth uses IAM, OAuth through AgentCore Identity or API keys. Defaults are 200 TPS and 100 targets, owners can set rate limits, and calls cost $0.005 per 1,000.

The AgentCore harness is AWS's managed agent loop in AgentCore, GA since 2026-06-17. You define a model, system prompt and tools with CreateHarness and call InvokeHarness, and each session runs in an isolated microVM with a filesystem and shell. Since November 2026 its defaults use Strands with Claude Opus 5. AWS recommends it as the migration target from Bedrock Agents Classic, and Step Functions has an optimized integration for it.

AgentCore Identity is AWS's agent identity and credential vault, providing workload identities, OAuth2 and API-key credential providers and a token vault, and it works with Cognito, Okta, Entra ID and Auth0. Agents call GetWorkloadAccessTokenForJWT, and outbound OAuth supports M2M and three-legged USER_FEDERATION flows. 2026 added on-behalf-of token exchange, private IdP egress, Private Key JWT, Secrets Manager references and a Consent Portal. It costs $0.010 per 1,000 requests, with no charge through Runtime or Gateway.

AgentCore Memory is AWS's short-term and long-term memory service for agents. It added episodic memory, IngestData and TTL on long-term records, and short-term memory moved to consumption pricing in October 2026. Custom strategies need a role passed in memoryExecutionRoleArn that trusts bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com. Limits include 150 resources per Region and 200 CreateEvent calls per second per account.

AgentCore Payments is AWS's AgentCore service for agent microtransactions over x402 and the Machine Payments Protocol, using Coinbase CDP and Stripe (Privy) wallets. It has been in preview since May 2026 and is available in only a few Regions, which have not been confirmed.

AgentCore Policy is AWS's authorization layer for agent-to-tool calls, GA since March 2026: policy engines attached to an AgentCore Gateway evaluate every tool call, deny by default and run in ENFORCE or LOG_ONLY mode. Policies are written in Cedar (now called Dogwood, Cedar-compatible) or natural language converted to Cedar, and Bedrock Guardrails are supported. Fixed limits include 1,000 engines, a 400 KB schema cap per engine and 5 TPS for CreatePolicy, and it costs $0.000025 per authorization request.

AgentCore Runtime is AWS's serverless host for agents and MCP servers, running containers or direct code in microVMs, or on the Instances compute type, over the HTTP, MCP, A2A and AG-UI protocols. Inbound auth is SigV4 or JWT, not both. It needs an execution role, creates a workload identity for each agent, and can be restricted to calls from your gateway. Limits include 1,000 TPS data-plane and 25 TPS new sessions per account, 8-hour sessions and 100 MB payloads.

Amazon Bedrock Agents Classic is AWS's original managed agents feature. It has been in maintenance mode and closed to new customers since 2026-07-30, with no new features and no end-of-life date. AWS recommends migrating to the AgentCore harness or to AgentCore Runtime, and a migration skill is in the Agent Toolkit for AWS. Custom service roles need model, S3 schema, knowledge base and optional guardrail permissions, and action-group Lambda functions need resource policies that allow Bedrock to invoke them.

Amazon Bedrock API keys are bearer tokens (AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK) for tools that can't use SigV4, and they also work with the OpenAI SDK. Short-term keys inherit the caller's IAM permissions and last up to 12 hours, while long-term keys create an IAM user with AmazonBedrockLimitedAccess and are meant only for exploration. AWS recommends STS credentials instead, and admins can deny keys with SCPs or the bedrock:BearerTokenType condition. Token-generator libraries exist for Python and JavaScript.

bedrock-mantle is an Amazon Bedrock inference endpoint (bedrock-mantle.{region}.api.aws) that serves the Responses, Chat Completions and Messages APIs at the same per-token price as bedrock-runtime. It alone supports server-side tools, background inference, Projects and Workspaces. Its IAM action is bedrock-mantle:CreateInference, and it has its own quota pool with separate input and output TPM and no RPM. Anthropic models called here need no First Time Use form, and a wrong /v1 or /openai/v1 path prefix makes requests fail.

bedrock-runtime is AWS's recommended Amazon Bedrock inference endpoint, serving InvokeModel, Converse, the Anthropic Messages API, and OpenAI-compatible Responses and Chat Completions at /openai/v1. It alone supports Guardrails, prompt routing, custom inference profiles, batch and Provisioned Throughput. All its APIs share one quota per model and Region, separate from bedrock-mantle, and listing models against /openai/v1 returns a 404.

Amazon Bedrock cross-Region inference routes requests through geographic profiles (prefixes like us and eu) that stay within a geography, or global profiles that route to any commercial Region, each with its own quota pool managed in the source Region. IAM must allow the profile and each destination model, plus the Region-agnostic ARN for global profiles. Region-deny SCPs cause AccessDeniedException unless they allow destination Regions or use the bedrock:InferenceProfileArn exemption.

Amazon Bedrock Guardrails is AWS's content safety layer for model calls; IAM or SCPs can require a specific guardrail with bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier. Organization-level enforcement from the management account has been GA since April 2026, the most restrictive control wins, and Standard-tier org guardrails need resource-based policies. AgentCore Policy supports Guardrails, and Agents Classic maintenance mode doesn't affect them. Pricing is per 1,000 text units, for example $0.15 for content filters, and regex and word filters are free.

Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base is AWS's fully managed RAG service, GA since June 2026 in eight Regions, including GovCloud. It manages vector storage and offers hybrid search, reranking and agentic multi-hop retrieval. It has six native connectors (S3, SharePoint, Confluence, Google Drive, OneDrive and Web Crawler) and integrates natively with AgentCore. Pricing is $5 per GB per month and $1 per 1,000 standard retrievals.

Amazon Q Developer is AWS's AI coding assistant. Its CLI and IDE became Kiro in November 2025, and in November 2026 the AWS Console version was renamed AWS assistant. The Free tier, which includes 50 agentic requests per month, may use content for service improvement, while Pro does not. Opt-out uses an AWS Organizations AI services opt-out policy or IDE settings.

Amazon Quick is AWS's agentic workspace product, formerly Amazon Quick Suite. It was renamed AWS Quick in a What's New post dated 2026-11-09, and customers don't need to take any action. AWS Quick is the current name.

Amazon Quick Suite is the AWS agentic workspace that replaced Amazon QuickSight and launched as GA in October 2025. It was later renamed Amazon Quick and then, in November 2026, AWS Quick, which is its current name.
